sources.citation: D.O. Hebb (2005). The Organization of Behavior.
sources.notes: Foundational primary work — 1949 foundational monograph The Organization of Behavior (2005 edition) — establishing the core empirical observations and theoretical framework.

sources.citation: T. V. P. Bliss, Terje Lømo (1973). Long-lasting potentiation of synaptic transmission in the dentate area of the anaesthetized rabbit following stimulation of the perforant path. The Journal of Physiology.
sources.notes: Landmark physiological demonstration of hippocampal long-term potentiation (LTP) following brief high-frequency perforant-path stimulation.

sources.citation: Jungwoo Kang (2016). Historical figures in neuroscience: Donald Hebb. Cambridge Medicine Journal.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2016) in Cambridge Medicine Journal extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Guo-qiang Bi, Mu-ming Poo (1998). Synaptic Modifications in Cultured Hippocampal Neurons: Dependence on Spike Timing, Synaptic Strength, and Postsynaptic Cell Type. Journal of Neuroscience.
sources.notes: Maps the millisecond asymmetric window of spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), distinguishing causal pre-before-post LTP from post-before-pre LTD.

sources.citation: Luc Granger (1992). Prix Donald O. Hebb honorant une contribution remarquable à la psychologie en tant que science/The 1991 Donald O. Hebb Award for distinguished contribution to psychology as a science. Canadian Psychology / Psychologie canadienne.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1992) in Canadian Psychology / Psychologie canadienne extending the foundational findings.
